newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee higher on NY, July stalls at $1,700.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee higher on NY, July stalls at $1,700.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures kept most of their early gains by Monday midsession but further advance was capped by origin sales at the highs.
Benchmark July, gapping $14 higher at the open against pre-market expectations of $20 up, was driven much higher but failed to pierce the closely-watched resistance at $1,700, the intraday peak.
It still closed $36 higher at $1,698 a tonne.

The gains were widely expected after another strong New York performance on Friday. The market scored sharp gains for three days in a row on the back of worries of the high open interest in May and the low level of deliverable coffee.
May's first notice day is April 22. London traders called New York to open unchanged on Monday.
News Colombian truck drivers started a nationwide strike on Sunday could give further support to the market as sizeable April coffee was still awaiting shipments.
In London, the strike news had little impact this morning with one trader saying that a lot of coffee cargoes could have been rushed to the ports ahead of the strike.
Some also thought that the new strike was likely to be less disruptive than the crippling stoppage in January.
But broker GNI said around 200,000 to 350,000 bags of April shipments were still to be loaded.
It said while the government had threatened to declare the strike illegal, this did not stop the worker action in January.
By the close, midday volume in London reached 2,359 lots. The bulk of London's activity was centred on fund moving out their May positions to July.
Traders detected no fresh fund interest.
In other stories, Brazil trade house Tristao put Brazil 1996/97 crop estimate at 27.5 million bags, up from its previous forecast of 25.85 million. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
